Of Typhos. Thus M: παρήορον [hanging beside] in many copies, which form Homer and others used. Similarly in several other words the tragedians preferred the Doric a to the Ionic η. Hesychius explains παράορος [hanging beside] by σειραφόρος [trace-horse].
And now his useless and outspread body lies near the sea-washed strait.
